messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
I'm pretty new at this. Target apogee is around 175 m. Motor class B at most. Thanks for the help!

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Around 175 m means 166 to 184 m. Motor class B at most, so nothing above a B. No wind, rail, site, or landing number, so 2 m/s, 1.5 m, sea level, and 6 m/s. Drag-free speed for 175 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 175) = 59 m/s.
2. Feasibility: A C is already too much motor and it is over the class cap anyway. A B on a light 18 mm rocket is the right size. An A is the fallback if the B overshoots.

2. Feasibility: Estes B6 is class B, 4.3 N*s, 5.2 N, 0.83 s, 18 mm by 0.07 m, 0.0156 kg, and the only delay is 0 s, so the chute has to be electronic or it opens at burnout. The B4 came back as class C, 5.1 N*s, so it is over the cap. The A8 is class A, 2.2 N*s, half of the B. On a guessed 0.04 kg rocket, thrust-to-weight is 5.2 / (0.04 * 9.81) = 13.3.
3. Size: For 0.045 kg at 4 m/s the chute is 2 * 0.045 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 4^2) = 0.056 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.056 / 3.1416) = 0.27 m. I will use 0.30 m. Tube 0.024 m outer, mount 0.020 m, clear of the 0.018 m case and nowhere near a large airframe.
4. Draft: Cardboard ogive 0.07 m on a 0.28 m cardboard tube, outer diameter 0.024 m, wall 1 mm. B6 plugged, 0.30 m chute at apogee. Three birch fins, root 0.055 m, tip 0.025 m, span 0.04 m, sweep 0.025 m, 3 mm. Sea-level defaults.

4. Check: The simulator gives 161.0 m, just under the 166 m floor of about 175 m. The rest passes: rail exit 21.9 m/s, thrust-to-weight 8.9, margin 1.8 cal at the rail and through the burn, landing 3.9 m/s, chute at 5.7 s. Mass 0.0594 kg. There is margin to spare, so a little fin drag can come off.
5. Fix: 161.0 m is the miss. Span goes from 0.04 m to 0.032 m and root from 0.055 m to 0.048 m, tip 0.022 m. Motor, tube, and chute stay.

4. Check: The simulator gives 173.9 m, inside 166 to 184 m. Rail exit 23.3 m/s, thrust-to-weight 9.3, margin 1.56 cal at the rail and through the burn, landing 3.8 m/s, chute at 5.9 s. Mass 0.0567 kg.
5. Fix: 173.9 m is in band and the gates pass, so the fins stay.
6. Uncertainty: A B this light will lose metres if the chute or the altimeter is heavier than 0.0567 kg. Cd 0.8 on a 0.30 m plastic chute is optimistic, so the real landing may be a little faster than 3.8 m/s and still under 6. The motor only offers a 0 s delay, so this flight depends on the altimeter actually opening the chute at apogee.
